title: The dyadic triangular Hilbert form
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that the dyadic triangular Hilbert form is bounded on L^3 x L^3 x L^3 uniformly in the scales and with no condition on the inputs: the sum over any finite set of scales of the absolute values of the local forms over admissible (XOR) triples of dyadic intervals is at most 40 times the product of the L^3 norms. This answers the dyadic question asked by Thiele. Step functions as matrices on atoms; the energy tr(P^(3/2)), its Hessian and its comparison under the order of matrices; a dimension-free bound for the trace of a triangle of matrices and contractions by three Hessian forms; the energy of an admissible triple grows under splitting into its four children by a multiple of its local form, and the increases telescope.
prerequisites: linear algebra over R: symmetric matrices, the spectral theorem, positive semidefinite order, the trace; the inverse function theorem in finite dimensions
the Lebesgue integral, L^p spaces and Holder's inequality, as in Fremlin's Measure Theory (core course Measure and Integration)

checks.reading: The manuscript 'An L^3 bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form' (OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026; build/main.tex and the sections introduction, matrix, trace, dyadic, summation and history, 29 kB of TeX; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: the product G of the three inputs is named; the children of an admissible triple and their sign distribution are stated as a lemma with proof; the scalar integral behind the monotonicity of the square root is computed; the order comparison uses the formula b_P(K) = (3/2) <K, L^{-1} K> of the Hessian lemma; the exercises check the definitions, the trace identity and the energy bound on small cases (one of them attains the bound for J_k). The matrix lemmas come from OpenAI's manuscript on the maximal triangular Hilbert transform (24 Sep 2026), whose own proofs this manuscript reproduces in the real case. Follow-up literature on 17 Oct 2026: an arXiv search for 'triangular Hilbert' found no later work; the most recent entry is Lin and Slavikova, arXiv:2607.20206 (rough averages).
